note: Candidate hypotheses generated before implementation (prompt requirement). Rank = qualitative expected DTI value per implementation cost. Only H-CPX-1 is this session's lane; the rest are queued, not run. 'Untried' is assessed against this repo's code/evidence and the restored registry's documented methods; a full history audit of ~100 external repos is not claimed.

hypotheses.name: Coincident potential-field x strain ridge posterior + kernel-exact expected-DTI emission
hypotheses.layers: iso_grav_anom, tmi, tmi_hg/vg, depth_to_base_surf, cond_surf, geod_2ndinv, geod_shearrate, det_elev (19-band stack) + shared 77-col cache for the supervised part
hypotheses.signature: Multi-scale Hessian ridge strength with cross-scale (sigma 1.0 vs 2.5) persistence, tilt-derivative zero-crossing edges, and doubled-angle gravity-vs-magnetic gradient orientation agreement; weakest-link/mean-rank coincidence across independent physics
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: Density, magnetic-basement, conductivity and strain boundaries continue beneath basin fill where surface mapping stops; requiring spatially coincident, orientation-agreeing ridges in independent fields targets through-going structure rather than catalogue proximity, and the label-free half of the surface cannot collapse onto mapped traces
hypotheses.difference: Prior lanes used single-field tilt/worm lineaments, supervised stacks alone, or fixed-spacing CELF coverage. None rank-fused a label-free multi-physics coincidence score with an OOF posterior, and none priced expected FP mass (alpha=0.2) into kernel-exact greedy placement
hypotheses.mimic: Buried caldera ring margins; tilted ash-flow tuff hogbacks; fan-channel margins; survey seams
hypotheses.cost: Medium (all inputs already local; new code = transforms + allocator)

hypotheses.name: Strain-fabric discontinuity corridors (orientation-coherence breaks in the geodetic strain tensor)
hypotheses.signature: Structure-tensor orientation field of the strain-rate invariants; score persistent linear breaks in orientation coherence at 1-3 km scale
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: Actively extending but unmapped faults localize interseismic strain; a coherent fabric break can extend beyond any mapped trace instead of rewarding catalogue distance
hypotheses.difference: Strain bands appear as generic HGB inputs in prior stacks, but no restored method extracts an orientation-discontinuity lineament field from them
hypotheses.mimic: Anthropogenic deformation (pumping, geothermal production), gridding/interpolation seams in the strain model

hypotheses.name: Conductive-basement step coincident with magnetic source-depth transition
hypotheses.layers: depth_to_base_surf, cond_surf, tmi vertical/horizontal gradients, rtp
hypotheses.signature: Paired step edges: lateral gradient ridge of basement depth/conductivity within 1 px of a magnetic gradient ridge, sustained over >=1 km along strike
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: A faulted basement contact juxtaposes conductive basin fill against resistive basement and offsets magnetic sources; the paired step can be traced under cover far from mapped surface breaks
hypotheses.difference: Conductivity/basement used as point features before; an explicit two-field paired-step coincidence with along-strike persistence is new in this repo
hypotheses.mimic: Non-faulted basement lithologic contacts; basin-margin onlap; inversion artefacts in the depth surface

hypotheses.name: Gravity-strain boundary intersection nodes as stepover targets
hypotheses.signature: Intersections and acute junctions of independent gravity-gradient and strain ridges (Andersonian stepover/dilation sites), scored by junction angle and dual-ridge strength
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: Releasing stepovers and fault intersections localize geothermal upflow and are preferentially missed where each individual strand is short or buried; node-targeting differs from tracing whole lineaments
hypotheses.difference: Tip/stepover analogues were derived from catalogue geometry (GEMSDOE33); deriving nodes purely from geophysical ridge networks is different
hypotheses.mimic: Crossing lithologic contacts; intersecting survey lineaments without faulting

hypotheses.name: Hydrochemical geothermometer residual corridors
hypotheses.layers: GDR submission 1391 spring/well chemistry + 2 m temperature probes (already mirrored as point features) conditioned on elevation/lithology background
hypotheses.signature: Spatially coherent positive temperature/silica residuals after background regression, terminating or aligning along independent potential-field axes
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: Blind geothermal upflow requires permeable structure; residual corridors can flag faults with no surface/geophysical expression at 100 m
hypotheses.difference: Probe/thermal layers exist as smoothed point-density features; a background-conditioned residual-corridor test has not been run
hypotheses.mimic: Shallow groundwater flow, mixing/evaporation, seasonal sampling bias, pumping
hypotheses.cost: High; sparse point support limits pixel-level DTI value
hypotheses.external_data_needed: Free official source: OpenEI Geothermal Data Repository submission 1391 (https://gdr.openei.org/submissions/1391) - already mirrored in-repo via DOI-pinned zips in the shared cache, so obtainable without credentials; deferred on cost/benefit, not access
